title: Low-jitter Ingress Gateway for Console Telemetry
creator: Emily Chen
description: Problem: Console telemetry ingestion currently sees high tail latency and jitter during bursty user events (UI releases, customer load tests). Upstream producers (SDKs/clients) emit variable-sized batches which cause hot partitions and spikes in downstream CPU/GC. This ticket proposes an ingress gateway component that smooths bursts, provides adaptive coalescing, assigns stable idempotency keys, and emits enriched envelope metadata for routing and debugging. Objectives: 1) keep 99th percentile end-to-end pipeline ingress < 150ms under steady load and < 400ms during 10x burst for typical request sizes; 2) avoid creating hotspots by adaptive partition keys; 3) provide observability hooks (per-tenant queue depth, retry counters, per-batch sizes).
acceptance_criteria: Ingress gateway deployed behind existing load balancer accepting console telemetry over HTTP/ gRPC
Adaptive coalescing reduces small-message overhead by >= 30% in controlled bench tests
Per-tenant tail latency (p99) meets SLO targets in canary: < 150ms steady, < 400ms at 10x bursts
Gateway emits provenance headers (internal_request_id, input_shard_hint, coalesce_window_ms) and writes metrics to console-telemetry-observability namespace
E2E compatibility: downstream processors (Kafka/KStream consumer groups) ingest without schema changes and handle idempotency via provided idempotency_key header
design_decisions: Use a dedicated ingress gateway service rather than client-side batching to centralize policy and observability
Implement adaptive coalescing using a token-bucket + max-window heuristic to balance latency vs throughput
Prefer partition hints over fixed tenant hash to reduce hot partitioning during bursts

Idempotency keys generated at gateway using stable hashing of (tenant_id, session_id, sequence_number) with 64-bit checksum to enable at-least-once to behave like once semantics for downstream dedupers
tradeoffs: Centralized gateway adds one hop and operational surface but enables unified telemetry enrichment and consistent SLO enforcement
Adaptive coalescing can increase median latency slightly for tiny events but reduces backend load and cost — acceptable for telemetry use-case
Choosing HTTP/gRPC ingress keeps SDK integration simple but requires conservative timeouts and connection pooling tuning
updates: 2026-02-16: Spike completed comparing Kafka vs Pulsar as the immediate durable buffer; decided to keep existing Kafka cluster to minimize migration risk
2026-02-20: Prototype gateway that supports HTTP/1.1 and gRPC; initial bench shows 35% reduction in CPU for downstream consumers with 10ms coalesce window
2026-02-25: Design review with Marcus Li and Sofia Martinez. Feedback: expose coalescing config via per-tenant policy and add per-request route for high-priority traffic (no coalescing)
2026-02-28: Implemented idempotency_key header generation and added unit tests for checksum collisions; opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ingress/pull/214

2026-03-01: Canary deploy to staging cluster (canary=5% tenants). Observability dashboard created: https://internal.redwood.ai/dashboards/console-ingress-canary showing p50/p95/p99 and per-tenant queue depth
review_feedback: Hannah O'Neill: Suggest exposing a diagnostics endpoint that can return a sample of coalesced bundle metadata for debugging without leaking payloads
SRE: Add circuit-breaker to fail-open to passthrough mode if gateway experiences overload to avoid blocking producer clients
Privacy team: ensure idempotency_key uses non-identifying inputs and is hashed; confirmed compliance with current PII guidelines
implementation_notes: Gateway implemented in Go for low-latency and small memory footprint; uses a few worker goroutines per core to avoid global mutexes
Uses resident ring buffer per-tenant with configurable max_coalesce_ms and max_batch_bytes
Backpressure strategy: if ring buffer full, apply priority-aware drop or fallback to passthrough (configurable per-tenant)
Integration tests include synthetic burst harness and backwards-compatibility tests against existing Kafka consumers
risks: Mis-tuned coalescing can mask upstream regression in SDKs — mitigated by having an opt-out route and per-tenant controls
Rolling out a new gateway may change request patterns to downstream consumers; we must coordinate with consumer teams and increment canary size slowly
Edge-case: very large single payloads must bypass coalescing to avoid head-of-line blocking—added explicit size threshold
next_steps: Complete canary run for two business days and collect SLO metrics
Address Hannah's diagnostic endpoint and SRE circuit-breaker comments (issue created)
Coordinate with consumer teams to validate idempotency handling and add consumer-side acceptance tests
